cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He's been talking about his own people, Israel, and how not all of them welcomed the good news (Romans 10:16). So now he asks it straight out: 'I ask then, did God reject His people?'

cards.question: True or false: Paul answers that yes, God has rejected His people Israel.
Paul says CERTAINLY NOT, then points to himself as an Israelite and a descendant of Abraham. Which tribe is Paul from?

cards.text: If God threw out Israel, He'd have to throw out the guy WRITING THE LETTER! Paul says God did not reject His people, whom He foreknew, and then he brings up Elijah, a prophet of Israel (1 Kings 18:36).

cards.question: Paul reminds them what the Scripture says about Elijah: he appealed to God ___ Israel.

cards.text: And Elijah does NOT hold back. He says, 'Lord, they have killed Your prophets and torn down Your altars.'

cards.question: Elijah tells God His prophets are killed and His altars are torn down. Then he tells God who's left. What does Elijah say?

answers.text: He is the only one left

cards.question: True or false: Elijah tells God that the people are seeking his life as well.

cards.text: Elijah's telling God he's the LAST cookie on the plate, and somebody's reaching for him. So Paul asks, 'And what was the divine reply to him?'

cards.question: God replies to Elijah, 'I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men…' What makes those seven thousand stand out?

answers.text: They have not bowed the knee to Baal
They have hidden all of God's prophets
They have rebuilt all of God's altars

cards.question: True or false: God's reply means Elijah was not the only one left who hadn't bowed the knee to Baal.

cards.text: Elijah's story wasn't just a trip down memory lane, friend. Paul says God is doing it the same way right now, in his own day.

cards.question: Like the seven thousand in Elijah's day, Paul says there is something at the present time. What is it?
Paul says this remnant is chosen by ___.

cards.text: So the remnant is chosen by grace. Now Paul sets grace right next to works, and he's got something to say about how the two go together.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the remnant is chosen partly by grace and partly by works.

cards.text: Paul says if it's by grace, it's no longer by works, or grace would no longer be grace. Grace you earn isn't a gift, friend, that's a PAYCHECK!
What then? Paul says what Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, like chasing a bus for three blocks and watching the doors close right in front of you.

cards.question: True or false: Israel failed to obtain what it was seeking, but Paul says the elect did obtain it.
And the rest of Israel? Paul says the others were ___.

cards.text: Paul doesn't leave that as his own opinion, friend. He backs it up with Scripture: 'God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear, to this very day.'

cards.question: Paul quotes Scripture about eyes that could not see and ears that could not hear. Which group in Israel is he describing?

answers.text: The seven thousand in Elijah's day

cards.text: Paul's stacking up witnesses like a lawyer in a courtroom, friend. Next up is David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), who says, 'May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution to them.'
David goes on, 'May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.' Heavy words, friend. I'm gonna let those sit in the oven a minute.

cards.question: True or false: David's line about eyes being darkened so they cannot see paints the same picture as the Scripture Paul quoted just before, about eyes that could not see.
